title: THE GENDER OF RELIGION
description: ENJOY PHILOSOPHY MEETS WEEKLY EVERY SUNDAY BETWEEN 11.30 AND 14.30 AT EDUARDO VII PARK, HERE:\*\* [https://goo.gl/maps/5e3jKFEweXkNvDdK6](https://goo.gl/maps/5e3jKFEweXkNvDdK6) **ITS THE GARDEN BETWEEN THE “CARLOS LOPES PAVILLION” AND THE “PRAIA NO PARQUE” RESTAURANT AT EDUARDO VII PARK.** THIS IS A GROUP FOR ANYONE INTERESTED IN ENJOYING PHILOSOPHY. NO PRIOR KNOWLEDGE IS REQUIRED. ONLY ETERNAL CURIOSITY AND THE PLEASURE OF KNOWLEDGE. PLS KEEP UPDATED of any changes and updates on our WhatsApp Group: [Enjoy Philosophy Lisbon Group Access-Link](https://chat.whatsapp.com/EgaLvlLCAbSL00cYmhpOSu) We will learn, debate, enjoy and investigate philosophers and diverse themes from the philosophical perspective. Each reunion is structured as a conversation among all attendees about that day s philosopher softly moderated by the organizer. The conversation will kick-off from the very brief suggested reading providing easy access to all attendees both to the philosopher and the conversation. Let´s be greek and dive today on… **the gender of Religion...** **The question quietly whispered by many and openly debated in different social forums, is painfully simple...** **Can Religion and Gender Equality co-exist in our societies ?** **The complexity of an issue that touches almost every fibre of our systems of beliefs is exemplified with appalling intensity in a French society torn apart by heated and unsolvable debates on how to fairly integrate their laïcist republican tradition with the very meaningful religious communities they host.** **Those debates, with their latent (and often explicit) violence can be described as a fundamental factor on how France´s political landscape is being shaped: this is not a far and abstract issue, resolved during the enlightenment and buried under the Nietzscheian "God is Dead". Not at all. God doesn't look very much dead indeed: we talk about a very concrete, present and critical topic infuencing the political realities of many countries. It´s hard to conceive the current French political map without the permanent presence of this debate during the last half a century.** **The traditional values of the 3 great monotheistic religions, very much aligned in their gender policies, conflict in a variety of aspects with those of the liberal western societies, but is in the Gender area where the clash becomes specially harsh... given the centrality of the Gender perspective evolution in modern liberal societies, and the huge road those new perspectives have walked and distanced themselves, therefore, from the religious positions. A seemingly unbridgeable distance, as often expressed by both the religious and the liberal perspectives.** **Nevertheless... in this millennial storm, a plethora of voices can be heard: defenders of compatibility point to egalitarian readings within Judaism, Christianity, Islam, and beyond — traditions of reform, mystical strands that dissolve hierarchy, theologians who argue that patriarchy was the culture surrounding the revelation rather than the revelation itself.** **Skeptics reply that you can reinterpret almost anything if you try hard enough, and that a tradition which needs to be heavily edited to pass a modern basic ethics test has already conceded the argument.** **The multicultural reality of our societies has turned this theoretical debate into a very practical one, where laws must be approved, education programs defined, etc...** **And beyond the specificity of the gender perspective, other relevant questions arise in this fire. From how our societies deal with "Radical Otherness" to the capacity of religions themselves to meaningfully change, adapt, learn, not only under the impositions of the "ideological market", but willingly, maturely, in case they want to mantain the role of "Ethical Guidance" they historically played.** **Let´s think about the confluence of 2 of the most meaningful institutions humanity as ever experienced: Religion and Gender Role attribution... and their (so far) inextricable relation... will that be so... also for the next 3000 years?**

Anyone interested in Product or trying to get into Product Management is welcome. Most AI initiatives don't fail at implementation. They fail before anyone writes a line of code or signs a vendor contract. The tools are bought, the use cases get announced, and six months later, no one can explain what changed. This session uses a real startup case study to walk through the discovery work most organizations skip: figuring out where AI belongs in a business before the building starts. It covers AI readiness assessment, where implementations break down, and what a structured pre-build process looks like in practice. About our speaker: Marvin McKinney has spent the last several years working inside that gap, adapting enterprise AI frameworks for businesses without dedicated ML teams or eight-figure transformation budgets. Before founding [Savvy Analytics](https://savvyanalytics.io), an AI and data strategy consultancy, he spent over a decade in analytics roles at Kroger, Bank of America, and GM Financial. He now brings that same Fortune 500 rigor to small and mid-sized companies, the ones with real AI ambition and no structured way to execute on it.
